The minimal reduction in staff suggests that banks are hesitant to make significant cuts and are anticipating a rebound in deal activity. [2, 3] The statement clarifies that all credit applicants are protected from discrimination based on protected characteristics such as national origin and race, regardless of their immigration status. [2] While the ECOA does not explicitly prohibit creditors from considering an applicant's immigration status, the agencies warned that its use is only permissible when necessary to ascertain the creditor's rights and remedies regarding repayment. [1, 2] The agencies cautioned that an unnecessary or overly broad reliance on immigration status, which may serve as a proxy for protected characteristics, could lead to illegal discrimination. [1, 4] This guidance was prompted by consumer reports of being denied various types of loans due to their immigration status, despite being otherwise qualified. [2, 3] <3> In the third quarter of 2023, loan growth at U.S. commercial banks was sluggish, increasing by only 0.7% from June 28 to September 27. [1] This trend was attributed to weaker demand and tighter lending standards, a view supported by Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michael Barr in a speech on October 2, 2023. [1] While overall loan growth was subdued, lending for credit cards saw a more significant increase of 2.4% during the same period. [1] The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) also reported moderated lending in the third quarter, with a 0.4% increase in total loans and an annual growth rate of 2.9%, citing lower loan demand and stricter underwriting. The financial results themselves were scheduled for release at approximately 7:00 a.m. (EDT) on the day of the call. The event proceeded as planned, with the company releasing its earnings report and holding the conference call on October 13, 2023, where it reported a net income of $13.2 billion for the quarter. <5> On September 11, 2023, at the Barclays Financial Services Conference, Bank of America's Chief Financial Officer, Alastair Borthwick, announced his expectation for the investment banking sector's fees to decrease by 30% to 35% in the third quarter of 2023 compared to the same period in the previous year. Despite the anticipated industry-wide downturn, Borthwick projected that Bank of America would outperform the sector average. He suggested that the bank's investment banking fees for the quarter could be approximately $1 billion. Borthwick also noted that income from the bank's global markets business was expected to see a low single-digit range increase compared to the prior year. <6> On July 27, 2023, US federal banking regulators issued proposals to significantly revise the risk-based regulatory capital requirements for banking organizations with $100 billion or more in total assets. The proposal is intended to implement the final components of the 2017 changes to international capital standards known as the Basel III agreement or "Endgame Standard." These new rules are expected to significantly increase the common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital requirements for most of the affected large and midsize US banks. <7> On June 28, 2023, the Federal Reserve released the results of its annual stress test, which found that all 23 large banks examined have sufficient capital to withstand a severe recession. [3, 7] In the hypothetical adverse scenario, the banks would be able to absorb a total of $541 billion in losses and continue to lend to households and businesses. [1] This year's test was noted as particularly significant following the failure of three U.S. banks earlier in the year and included a severe global recession with significant stress in commercial and residential real estate markets. [2, 3] The Bank Policy Institute noted that since 2020, the stress test no longer functions as a pass/fail exercise but is used to determine a capital charge added to each bank's minimum capital requirements. [5] <8> On June 12, 2023, Nasdaq announced it had entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Adenza, a provider of mission-critical risk management and regulatory software, from private equity firm Thoma Bravo. [5, 6] The deal, valued at $10.5 billion, consists of $5.75 billion in cash and 85.6 million shares of Nasdaq common stock. [3, 8] This acquisition is Nasdaq's largest to date and is a key part of its strategy to accelerate its transformation into a leading technology provider for the global financial system, expanding its portfolio in risk management and regulatory compliance. [1, 5] Adenza was formed by combining two major brands, Calypso and AxiomSL. [2, 6] [1, 4, 7] [3, 5]

Prediction target period: from 2025-04-13 to 2025-06-29. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On April 3, 2025, TowneBank and Old Point Financial Corporation jointly announced the signing of a definitive merger agreement for TowneBank to acquire Old Point in a transaction valued at approximately $203 million. [1, 2, 3] This proposed merger followed TowneBank's recent finalization of its acquisition of Village Bank and Trust Financial Corp., making the Old Point deal its second major acquisition in a short period. [4, 5] <2> In the first quarter of 2025, the U.S. IPO market showed signs of a tentative recovery, marking its most active start to a year since 2021. [6, 7] However, reports from various financial analysis firms present a mixed picture of the total number of IPOs and proceeds raised. One analysis from ICR noted 15 traditional IPOs raising nearly $8 billion, while a Renaissance Capital report cited 53 IPOs generating a combined $8.5 billion. [3] An EY report indicated 59 IPOs raised $8.9 billion. [1] Despite a strong start to the year, IPO activity slowed towards the end of the quarter. [3, 4] This slowdown was attributed to market uncertainty and volatility driven by concerns over inflation, potential tariff implementations, and shifting government policies. [1, 3, 4] <3> A report analyzing merger and acquisition (M&A) activity in the fourth quarter of 2024 concluded that while deal-making increased compared to 2023's subdued levels, the highly optimistic forecasts for a significant boom did not come to fruition. The report, published on February 18, 2025, identified geopolitical instability and persistently high interest rates as key factors that negatively impacted the market. In the United States, M&A volumes for the year ending December 31, 2024, saw a 10% rise, reaching a total of $1.55 trillion. <4> The Federal Reserve's transition of the Fedwire Funds Service to the ISO 20022 message format is a significant regulatory change aimed at enhancing the efficiency of domestic and cross-border payments through greater interoperability and richer data. While the original compliance deadline was March 10, 2025, the Federal Reserve announced on February 13, 2025, that it would reschedule the implementation to July 14, 2025. This decision was made in response to industry requests and to provide financial institutions and vendors with additional time to prepare their systems. The extension was seen as a relief by many in the industry who felt they were prepared only for a 'bare-minimum' launch. The new standard will also apply to wiring federal tax payments to the IRS. <5> In February 2025, Goldman Sachs rescinded its 2020 policy that required companies it took public in the U.S. and Western Europe to have at least two diverse board members. The bank cited legal and regulatory shifts as the reason for the change, specifically a U.S. Court of Appeals ruling in December 2024 that struck down Nasdaq's board diversity disclosure requirements. A spokesperson for Goldman Sachs stated that while the formal policy was ending, the bank continues to believe that diverse backgrounds and perspectives on boards are beneficial and will encourage companies to pursue them. The move is part of a broader trend of corporations reassessing their Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) initiatives following changes in the political and legal landscape. <6> In January 2025, the U.S. banking sector's merger and acquisition activity remained subdued with 11 deals announced, totaling a combined value of $678.4 million. [1] This represented a decrease from the 12 deals announced in January 2024, but an increase in total value from the previous year's $566.7 million. [1] Among the deals announced were Kalispell, Montana-based Glacier Bancorp Inc.'s acquisition of Bank of Idaho Holding Co. for $245.4 million and Clearfield, Pennsylvania-based CNB Financial Corp.'s purchase of ESSA Bancorp Inc. for $209.3 million. [1] The month also saw the first credit union-bank deal of 2025, with Frontwave CU acquiring Community Valley Bank for $56.4 million. [1] Overall, deal activity continued to build on the rebound seen in 2024, with analysts predicting a further increase in M&A throughout 2025. [3, 4] <7> Financial Institutions, Inc. executed a significant restructuring of its investment securities portfolio in December 2024 as part of a strategic balance sheet transformation. The company sold $653.5 million of available-for-sale investment securities at a pre-tax loss of $100.2 million. [1, 5] The net proceeds were then reinvested into higher-yielding agency-wrapped investment securities, increasing the weighted average yield from 1.74% to 5.16%. [1] This action was part of the company's Q4 2024 results, which were publicly announced on January 30, 2025. [1, 3] The restructuring was noted to be a driver of meaningful net interest margin expansion in subsequent quarters. [5] <8> The Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) published its 2025 Annual Regulatory Oversight Report on January 28, 2025. [1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] This resource offers member firms insights and observations from FINRA's various programs to help them strengthen their compliance procedures. [1, 5] The report covers 24 topics, highlighting both new and ongoing areas of focus. [1] Key emerging topics include risks associated with Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, and regulatory considerations for crypto assets. [1, 5] Ongoing priorities detailed in the report include cybersecurity, anti-money laundering (AML), and compliance with Regulation Best Interest (Reg BI). [1, 2] For 2025, FINRA added new sections on the third-party risk landscape, registered index-linked annuities (RILAs), and extended hours trading. [2, 3, 7, 8]

Prediction target period: from 2025-08-31 to 2025-11-16. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced on August 21, 2025, that Judge Margaret 'Meg' Ryan has been appointed as the new Director of the Division of Enforcement. Judge Ryan, a senior judge on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces, succeeds Sam Waldon, who was serving as Acting Director and will resume his role as Chief Counsel for the Division. SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins stated that Judge Ryan brings decades of experience as a respected judge and legal practitioner. Prior to her judgeship, she was a partner at the law firms Wiley Rein & Fielding LLP and Bartlit Beck Herman Palenchar & Scott LLP, and she also served as a law clerk for Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas. <2> T-Mobile has completed its acquisition of most of U.S. Cellular's wireless operations for approximately $4.4 billion. The deal includes U.S. Cellular's more than four million customers, its retail stores, and about 30% of its spectrum assets. This acquisition is expected to enhance T-Mobile's network, particularly in rural and underserved areas, by integrating U.S. Cellular's coverage. U.S. Cellular customers will be able to transition to T-Mobile plans. Following the transaction, U.S. Cellular will retain its tower assets and the remaining spectrum, rebranding as Array Digital Infrastructure, Inc. <3> On July 30, 2025, the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets (PWG) published a 166-page report titled "Strengthening American Leadership in Digital Financial Technology," in response to Executive Order 14178. The report provides a roadmap with recommendations for Congress and federal regulators to modernize the U.S. digital asset regulatory framework. Key areas covered include establishing a clear market structure with defined jurisdiction between the SEC and CFTC, modernizing banking and payments, countering illicit finance, and updating taxation policies for digital assets. The report advocates for an end to "regulation by enforcement" and encourages the use of rulemaking and exemptive authorities to foster innovation and the trading of digital assets. <4> Palo Alto Networks has announced its intention to acquire identity security leader CyberArk for approximately $25 billion. [3] The definitive agreement, which was announced on July 30, 2025, specifies that CyberArk shareholders will receive $45.00 in cash and 2.2005 shares of Palo Alto Networks common stock for each of their shares. [1, 5] This deal marks Palo Alto Networks' official entry into the identity security market, a move intended to establish identity security as a new core pillar of its platform strategy. [1, 6] The acquisition is part of a larger consolidation trend in the technology and cybersecurity sectors and is considered one of the largest M&A deals in the industry to date, following deals like Google's acquisition of Wiz and Cisco's of Splunk. [3, 4, 7] Analysts note that the move addresses a significant gap in Palo Alto Networks' portfolio, allowing it to offer a more comprehensive security platform that covers everything from network security to the increasingly critical area of identity management for human, machine, and AI agents. [4, 7] The deal is expected to close in the second half of Palo Alto Networks' fiscal year 2026, pending regulatory and shareholder approval. [2, 3] <5> On July 29, 2025, Union Pacific Corporation announced its agreement to acquire Norfolk Southern Corporation for an enterprise value of $85 billion. The deal, a mix of cash and stock, would create the first single transcontinental railroad in the United States, with a combined network of over 50,000 miles of track across 43 states. The new entity would connect approximately 100 ports from the East to the West Coast, aiming to streamline the U.S. supply chain and enhance freight service. The proposed merger is subject to approval from the Surface Transportation Board and shareholders of both companies, with the companies targeting a completion date in early 2027. The deal faces skepticism from the largest rail labor organization, the SMART Transportation Division, which has raised concerns about potential impacts on worker safety and rail service operations. <6> Baker Hughes announced it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Chart Industries, a global leader in process technologies and engineered equipment for handling gas and liquid molecules. The all-cash transaction is valued at an enterprise value of $13.6 billion, including debt. This acquisition aims to enhance Baker Hughes' presence in high-growth markets such as liquified natural gas (LNG), data centers, New Energy, and decarbonization. The boards of both companies have unanimously approved the deal, which is anticipated to close by mid-2026, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals. <7> On July 24, 2025, Pinnacle Financial Partners and Synovus Financial Corp. announced they entered into a definitive agreement to merge in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $8.6 billion. This merger will create a major regional bank focused on high-growth markets in the Southeast. The combined holding company will be named Pinnacle Financial Partners and be headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, while the bank, operating as Pinnacle Bank, will be based in Nashville, Tennessee. Under the terms, which were unanimously approved by both companies' boards, Synovus shareholders will own about 48.5% and Pinnacle shareholders will own about 51.5% of the new entity. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2026, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals. Until the merger is complete, both banks will continue to operate independently. <8> Pinnacle Financial Partners and Synovus Financial Corp. announced a definitive agreement for an $8.6 billion all-stock merger of equals, which is the largest bank-on-bank transaction of 2025. The combined entity will operate under the Pinnacle Financial Partners name and brand. As of June 30, 2025, Pinnacle had approximately $54.8 billion in assets, while Synovus had about $61 billion in assets, creating a combined company with over $115 billion in assets. Following the merger, Pinnacle shareholders will own approximately 51.5% of the new company, and Synovus shareholders will own about 48.5%. The deal will create the largest bank holding company in Georgia and the largest bank in Tennessee. The transaction, which has been unanimously approved by the boards of both companies, is expected to close in the first quarter of 2026, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals. <9> A Q2 2025 review of the financial sector highlighted several regulatory shifts that largely occurred in March 2025. [1] Key among these was a revision to the Corporate Transparency Act (CTA) via an interim final rule issued by the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN); sources point to the rule being issued on either March 21 or March 26, 2025, to recalibrate the definition of a "reporting company". [3, 6, 7] Another significant change was the new "two-strike" rule for payday lenders, a provision of the CFPB’s Small Dollar Lending Rule, which took effect on March 30, 2025. [5, 8, 9] This rule mandates that lenders must cease withdrawal attempts after two consecutive failures and obtain new borrower authorization before trying again. [5, 8] Additionally, FinCEN issued new Geographic Targeting Orders (GTOs) on March 11, 2025, which became effective on April 14, 2025. [2] These orders require money service businesses along the U.S.-Mexico border to file reports for transactions at a lowered $200 threshold. [2]

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In a monthly M&A report for September 2025, EY announced that U.S. deal value experienced a significant surge, with 151 large deals amounting to $257.6 billion. This increase was primarily driven by private equity, which accounted for approximately 60% of the value for deals over $100 million. This represents a sharp rise from PE's 45% share in August 2025, indicating a notable shift in the dynamics of U.S. dealmaking. <2> On October 15, 2025, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced its preliminary conditional approval for Erebor Bank, National Association, in Columbus, Ohio, to receive a de novo national bank charter. Backed by prominent tech investors including Peter Thiel, Palmer Luckey, and Joe Lonsdale, Erebor Bank aims to be a digital-native, full-service insured national bank. The bank's stated mission is to serve the "United States innovation economy" by targeting technology companies and high- and ultra-high-net-worth individuals utilizing virtual currencies. Its focus areas include digital assets, artificial intelligence, defense, and advanced manufacturing. The approval is notable as it is the first de novo bank charter to receive preliminary conditional approval under Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould, who stated the decision demonstrates that the OCC does not impose "blanket barriers" to banks engaging in digital asset activities, provided they are conducted in a "safe and sound manner." <3> A retrospective analysis of the investment banking industry for Q3 2025 reveals a period of significant growth, primarily driven by a surge in the value of mergers and acquisitions and robust performance from sales and trading divisions. Global M&A deal value increased substantially, with year-over-year growth reported between 36% and 40%, pushing the quarterly total to between $371 billion and over $1 trillion across different reports. This increase in value occurred despite the total number of transactions declining to a two-decade low, as the quarter was marked by a record number of mega-deals exceeding $10 billion. Investment banking fees saw a corresponding jump of 42% to $2.7 billion. Concurrently, Sales & Trading divisions provided a strong revenue anchor, with one major bank reporting a 21% increase in fixed-income trading fees to $5.6 billion and a 33% jump in equity trading fees to $3.3 billion. <4> Raymond James Financial Inc. announced its acquisition of a majority stake in GreensLedge Holdings LLC, a boutique investment bank specializing in structured credit and securitization. Founded in 2008, GreensLedge is recognized for its expertise in arranging complex financial instruments such as CLOs, CDOs, and ABS. This strategic move is designed to enhance Raymond James' capital markets and advisory platform by integrating GreensLedge's specialized capabilities with its own extensive fixed-income distribution and trading network. The acquisition formalizes a long-standing relationship between the two firms. Under the agreement, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Group, an existing partner of GreensLedge, will retain a minority interest in the company. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In a monthly M&A report for September 2025, EY announced that U.S. deal value experienced a significant surge, with 151 large deals amounting to $257.6 billion. This increase was primarily driven by private equity, which accounted for approximately 60% of the value for deals over $100 million. This represents a sharp rise from PE's 45% share in August 2025, indicating a notable shift in the dynamics of U.S. dealmaking. <2> On October 15, 2025, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced its preliminary conditional approval for Erebor Bank, National Association, in Columbus, Ohio, to receive a de novo national bank charter. Backed by prominent tech investors including Peter Thiel, Palmer Luckey, and Joe Lonsdale, Erebor Bank aims to be a digital-native, full-service insured national bank. The bank's stated mission is to serve the "United States innovation economy" by targeting technology companies and high- and ultra-high-net-worth individuals utilizing virtual currencies. Its focus areas include digital assets, artificial intelligence, defense, and advanced manufacturing. The approval is notable as it is the first de novo bank charter to receive preliminary conditional approval under Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould, who stated the decision demonstrates that the OCC does not impose "blanket barriers" to banks engaging in digital asset activities, provided they are conducted in a "safe and sound manner." <3> A retrospective analysis of the investment banking industry for Q3 2025 reveals a period of significant growth, primarily driven by a surge in the value of mergers and acquisitions and robust performance from sales and trading divisions. Global M&A deal value increased substantially, with year-over-year growth reported between 36% and 40%, pushing the quarterly total to between $371 billion and over $1 trillion across different reports. This increase in value occurred despite the total number of transactions declining to a two-decade low, as the quarter was marked by a record number of mega-deals exceeding $10 billion. Investment banking fees saw a corresponding jump of 42% to $2.7 billion. Concurrently, Sales & Trading divisions provided a strong revenue anchor, with one major bank reporting a 21% increase in fixed-income trading fees to $5.6 billion and a 33% jump in equity trading fees to $3.3 billion. <4> Raymond James Financial Inc. announced its acquisition of a majority stake in GreensLedge Holdings LLC, a boutique investment bank specializing in structured credit and securitization. Founded in 2008, GreensLedge is recognized for its expertise in arranging complex financial instruments such as CLOs, CDOs, and ABS. This strategic move is designed to enhance Raymond James' capital markets and advisory platform by integrating GreensLedge's specialized capabilities with its own extensive fixed-income distribution and trading network. The acquisition formalizes a long-standing relationship between the two firms. Under the agreement, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Group, an existing partner of GreensLedge, will retain a minority interest in the company. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. <5> Major U.S. banks, including JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, and Citigroup, are scheduled to begin reporting their third-quarter (Q3) 2025 earnings on Tuesday, October 14, 2025. An outlook published on October 9, 2025, indicates that analysts are forecasting strong performance. This optimism is driven by a predicted recovery in investment banking fees, as companies increasingly engage in M&A and capital raising, alongside robust trading revenues generated from heightened volatility in equity and fixed income markets. <6> On October 7, 2025, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) jointly issued a notice of proposed rulemaking. The proposal aims to define the term "unsafe or unsound practice" under the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and to create uniform standards for issuing Matters Requiring Attention (MRAs) to the banks they supervise. This initiative is part of a broader effort by the banking agencies to refocus supervision on core, material financial risks rather than on policies, processes, or documentation. The proposed definition of an "unsafe or unsound practice" requires an action that goes against generally accepted standards of prudent operation and is likely to cause material financial harm to the institution or pose a significant risk to the Deposit Insurance Fund. The proposal would also standardize when and how examiners can issue MRAs and other supervisory communications. Comments on the proposal are due 60 days after its publication in the Federal Register. <7> A report from S&P Global Market Intelligence revealed that U.S. bank merger and acquisition activity surged to a four-year high in the third quarter of 2025. The firm reported 52 deals were announced, totaling an aggregate deal value of $16.63 billion. This marks the highest number of quarterly deals since the third quarter of 2021 and the largest total deal value since the fourth quarter of 2021. A significant transaction in the quarter was PNC Financial Services Group Inc.'s $4.04 billion acquisition of FirstBank Holding Co. Another analysis from Ankura presented slightly different figures for the same period, reporting 46 deals with a total value of $17.4 billion. <8> Bank of America announced a significant senior leadership restructuring on September 12, 2025, appointing Dean Athanasia and Jim DeMare as Co-Presidents. This strategic move is widely interpreted as a step in the succession planning for CEO Brian Moynihan, who has expressed his intention to continue leading the bank through the end of the decade. In their new roles, Athanasia and DeMare will oversee the bank's eight lines of business, working to drive long-term growth and returns. The appointments are seen as narrowing the field of potential successors to Moynihan. Alongside these changes, Alastair Borthwick was appointed Executive Vice President and will continue in his role as Chief Financial Officer. <9> On August 29, 2025, the Federal Reserve Board announced the final individual capital requirements for large banks, which are scheduled to become effective on October 1, 2025. These requirements, which are informed by the annual supervisory stress tests, mandate the minimum capital banks must hold to ensure they can absorb losses and continue lending during a severe economic downturn. The total capital requirement for each bank is composed of a minimum 4.5% ratio, a stress capital buffer of at least 2.5%, and, for the largest and most complex banks, a surcharge for global systemically important banks. <10> On August 25, 2025, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit remanded two SEC rules, 10c-1a and 13f-2, which were adopted in October 2023 to increase transparency in securities lending and short selling. In the case, National Association of Private Fund Managers v. SEC, the court determined that the SEC acted arbitrarily and capriciously by failing to consider the combined economic impact of the two interconnected rules. While the court upheld the SEC's statutory authority and notice-and-comment process, it sent the rules back to the agency for further economic analysis. The rules were remanded without vacatur, meaning they remain in effect pending the SEC's review, though compliance dates may be adjusted.
